title: Fire, Coral and Rift
question: How do islands come to exist in the middle of the water?
hook: Some islands are torn off continents, some are built by volcanoes, and some are the last high ground of a sunken continent.
idea: Islands form in several ways: split from continents, raised by hotspot volcanoes, cracked out of plates, or built by coral on sinking volcanoes.

beats.prompt: A tectonic plate creeps steadily over a hotspot that stays in one place, building volcanoes as it goes. What pattern of islands do you get?

choices.label: A line of islands that get older and more eroded away from the hotspot
A tight cluster of islands all the same age
choices.feedback: Tempting if you picture one eruption, but the moving plate spreads the volcanoes out over time.

choices.label: A single island that keeps growing larger forever
choices.feedback: The plate keeps moving, so each volcano is carried away and a new one forms over the hotspot.

choices.label: A ring of coral around one central lagoon
choices.feedback: That describes an atoll, which comes from coral growing on a sunken volcano.

beats.explain: Plates moving over a stationary hotspot leave a linear chain, with islands farther from the hotspot progressively older and more eroded; Hawaii is the young, still active end.

beats.prompt: Put the life of a coral island in order.
items: A volcanic island stands above the sea
The volcanic island sinks below the surface
Coral reefs grow on the sunken volcano
Coral islands encircle a central lagoon as an atoll
beats.explain: Coral reefs grow on volcanic islands that have submerged, and when the coral islands ring a central lagoon the island is called an atoll.

beats.prompt: Match each island group to how it formed.
pairs: May have split off by seafloor spreading
beats.explain: Island chains form in different ways: hotspots, plate fractures, separation from continents, or what is left of a shrinking, sinking continent.

beats.prompt: Sort each island type into its group.
items: Split from a continent by plate tectonics
Shares wildlife with the mainland it left
Grown into an atoll from coral reefs
Barrier island built from shoreline sediment
beats.explain: Continental islands were split from a continent and share its life; oceanic islands were never part of a continent and come from volcanoes, coral or sediment.
